disharmonies.title: God Classes
disharmonies.problem: God Classes take on too much responsibility,
disharmonies.solution: Extract related islands of functionality into separate classes.  Leave God classes that don't change often alone.

disharmonies.title: Data Classes
disharmonies.problem: Data Classes are dumb data holders that other classes rely on.
disharmonies.solution: Move the data/variable(s) to the same class as the operation.

disharmonies.title: Refused Parent Bequest
disharmonies.problem: Child class is large and often complex, but doesn't override or use many of the parent class's methods
disharmonies.solution:
Do one or more of the following:
- Extract the child class into a separate class. Move the methods that are used from the parent class into the child class.
- Make unused protected members private in the parent class.
- If a parent class has multiple children, move methods not used by all descendants to another class.

disharmonies.title: Intensive Coupling
disharmonies.problem: Method calls too many methods from a few unrelated classes (often in a separate package).
disharmonies.solution: Move the calling method to a class more closely related to the other classes that the original method can call.

disharmonies.title: Dispersed Coupling
disharmonies.problem: Method calls a few methods in many classes
disharmonies.solution: Reduce the size of the calling method.  Extract methods from the calling method into the target classes.

disharmonies.title: Shotgun Surgery
disharmonies.problem: Method is called by many methods in many classes
disharmonies.solution:
- Move the method closer to the calling classes (move the behavior closer to the data) if it is small.
- If it is a large method, treat it as a Brain Method and decompose it into two or more smaller methods.
